claims.text: Peds: empagliflozin, canagliflozin and dapagliflozin are used in children > 10 y w T2DM;
claims.quote: Empagliflozin, canagliflozin, and dapagliflozin are sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors used for children > 10 years of age with type 2 diabetes
claims.locator: Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes in Children and Adolescents › Pharmacologic treatment › Other antihyperglycemic medications in children

claims.text: empagliflozin ≥ 10 y: hypoglycemia risk higher regardless of insulin use.
claims.quote: In pediatric patients aged 10 years and older, the risk of hypoglycemia was higher with JARDIANCE regardless of insulin use
claims.locator: 5.3 Hypoglycemia with Concomitant Use with Insulin and Insulin Secretagogues

claims.text: Empagliflozin 10 mg PO QD in the Am;
claims.quote: 10 mg orally once daily in the morning, taken with or without food.

claims.text: for more glycemic control may increase to 25 mg daily.
claims.quote: For additional glycemic control, may increase to 25 mg orally once daily in patients tolerating 10 mg once daily.
JARDIANCE is not recommended for use to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus with an eGFR less than 30 mL/min/1.73 m 2 .
with a hypersensitivity to empagliflozin or any of the excipients in JARDIANCE, reactions such as angioedema have occurred

claims.text: Ketoacidosis, incl fatal cases, in T2DM.
claims.quote: There have been postmarketing reports of fatal events of ketoacidosis in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus using SGLT2 inhibitors, including JARDIANCE.
claims.locator: 5.1 Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Patients with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and Other Ketoacidosis

claims.quote: JARDIANCE can cause intravascular volume depletion which may sometimes manifest as symptomatic hypotension or acute transient changes in creatinine

claims.text: Serious GU infections incl. urosepsis, pyelonephritis and Fournier's gangrene.
claims.quote: Serious genitourinary infections, including urosepsis, pyelonephritis, and necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum (Fournier's gangrene, a rare life-threatening infection requiring urgent surgical intervention), have occurred

claims.text: Lower limb amputation imbalance in some SGLT2i studies.
claims.quote: In some clinical studies with SGLT2 inhibitors an imbalance in the incidence of lower limb amputation has been observed.
Coadministration of empagliflozin with diuretics resulted in increased urine volume and frequency of voids, which might enhance the potential for volume depletion.

claims.text: Insulin or secretagogue: more hypoglycemia; consider lowering their dose when starting.
claims.quote: Consider lowering the dosage of insulin secretagogue or insulin to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia when initiating JARDIANCE.

claims.text: May lower lithium levels (check lithium more often).
claims.quote: Concomitant use of an SGLT2 inhibitor with lithium may decrease serum lithium concentrations.
SGLT2 inhibitors increase urinary glucose excretion and will lead to positive urine glucose tests.

claims.text: B4 starting, assess renal funct and vol status and correct vol depletion.
claims.quote: Assess renal function before initiating and as clinically indicated. Assess volume status and correct volume depletion before initiating.

claims.text: Hold ± 3 days b4 surg or prolonged fasting if poss.
claims.quote: Withhold JARDIANCE for at least 3 days, if possible, prior to surgery or procedures associated with prolonged fasting.

claims.text: Know ketoacidosis Sx; stop and seek care if they occur.
claims.quote: Educate all patients on the signs and symptoms of ketoacidosis and instruct patients to discontinue JARDIANCE and seek medical attention immediately if signs and symptoms occur.
claims.locator: 5.1 Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Patients with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and Other Ketoacidosis
